# Decision Support Frameworks

> Published by: Aeimathes (2026-06-01)
> Maintained by: Aeimathes

---

## Overview

Senior engineers ต้องตัดสินใจภายใต้ความไม่แน่นอน — frameworks 2 ตัวนี้ช่วยคนละจุด:

| Framework | เหมาะกับ | จุดประสงค์ |
|-----------|---------|----------|
| **ADR** (Architecture Decision Records) | การตัดสินใจที่สำคัญ | บันทึก + justify ทำไมถึงเลือกแบบนี้ |
| **Pre-Mortem** | ก่อนเริ่ม project/sprint | ค้นหา risks ที่ซ่อนอยู่ก่อนเกิดขึ้นจริง |

---

## Part 1: Architecture Decision Records (ADR)

### 1.1 Origin

Michael Nygard นำเสนอใน blog post "Documenting Architecture Decisions" (2011) — แนวคิด: ทุกการตัดสินใจสถาปัตยกรรมที่สำคัญควรมีเอกสาร brief บันทึกไว้ในโค้ด

Martin Fowler อธิบายเพิ่มเติมที่: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ArchitectureDecisionRecord.html

### 1.2 Core Concept

> "ถ้าไม่เขียน ADR = อีก 6 เดือนข้างหน้าไม่มีใครรู้ว่าทำไมถึงเลือก architecture แบบนี้"

ADR = append-only log — ไม่แก้ record เดิม แต่สร้าง record ใหม่ที่ supersede ของเดิม

### 1.3 Nygard Format (Original)

```markdown
# [ADR-NNNN] [Title]

## Status
[Proposed | Accepted | Deprecated | Superseded by ADR-XXXX]

## Context
[ปัญหาที่กำลังเผชิญ สถานการณ์ constraints]

## Decision
[การตัดสินใจที่เลือก เขียนเป็น active voice]

## Consequences
[ผลที่ตามมา ทั้งดีและไม่ดี tradeoffs ที่ยอมรับ]
```

### 1.4 MADR Format (แนะนำสำหรับทีมใหม่)

MADR 4.0.0 (released September 2024) — เพิ่มส่วน Considered Options และ Pros/Cons ทำให้ reasoning ชัดขึ้น

```markdown
# [ADR-NNNN] [Title]

## Status
[Proposed | Accepted | Deprecated | Superseded by ADR-XXXX]

## Context and Problem Statement
[อธิบายปัญหาใน 2-3 ประโยค]

## Decision Drivers
* [Driver 1 — e.g. performance requirement]
* [Driver 2 — e.g. team expertise]

## Considered Options
* [Option A]
* [Option B]
* [Option C]

## Decision Outcome
Chosen option: "[Option X]", because [justification].

### Consequences
* Good: [positive outcome]
* Bad: [negative outcome / accepted tradeoff]

## Pros and Cons of the Options

### Option A
* Good: ...
* Bad: ...

### Option B
* Good: ...
* Bad: ...
```

**Citation**: adr/madr GitHub. https://github.com/adr/madr | MADR official site. https://adr.github.io/madr/

### 1.5 ADR Lifecycle States

```
Proposed → Accepted → Deprecated
              ↓
           Superseded by ADR-XXXX
```

| State | ความหมาย |
|-------|---------|
| **Proposed** | กำลัง review หรือรอ approval |
| **Accepted** | ตัดสินใจแล้ว ใช้งานอยู่ |
| **Deprecated** | ไม่ใช้แล้ว แต่ยังไม่มี replacement |
| **Superseded** | มี ADR ใหม่แทนแล้ว — link ไว้เสมอ |

### 1.6 เมื่อไหร่ควรเขียน ADR

เขียนเมื่อการตัดสินใจ:
- มี tradeoffs ที่ต้องอธิบาย
- มีผลกระทบระยะยาว (เปลี่ยนยาก)
- ทำให้คนในทีมเกิด "แล้วทำไม..." ในอนาคต
- เกี่ยวกับ technology choice, framework, pattern สำคัญ

ไม่ต้องเขียนเมื่อ: ตัดสินใจ tactical เล็กน้อย หรือ reversible ง่าย

**Citation**: AWS Architecture Blog. https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/master-architecture-decision-records-adrs-best-practices-for-effective-decision-making/

### 1.7 Best Practices

1. **เก็บใน source repository** — ที่ `docs/adr/` หรือ `doc/decisions/`
2. **Numbered sequentially** — ADR-0001, ADR-0002, ...
3. **Short and focused** — เขียนได้ใน 1 หน้า เน้น WHY ไม่ใช่ WHAT
4. **Timebox การ review** — ≤ 45 นาทีต่อ ADR
5. **Link related ADRs** — อ้างอิง ADR เดิมที่เกี่ยวข้อง
6. **Never edit accepted ADRs** — สร้าง ADR ใหม่ที่ supersede แทน

**Citation**: TechTarget 8 Best Practices. https://www.techtarget.com/searchapparchitecture/tip/4-best-practices-for-creating-architecture-decision-records | Microsoft Azure WAF. https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/architect-role/architecture-decision-record

### 1.8 Tools

| Tool | ประเภท | URL |
|------|--------|-----|
| **npryce/adr-tools** | CLI — สร้าง/link ADR ใน markdown | https://github.com/npryce/adr-tools |
| **adr/madr** | Template + CLI (`npx madr`) | https://github.com/adr/madr |
| **Log4brains** | Static site generator — browsable ADR site | https://github.com/thomvaill/log4brains |
| **ADR Manager** | Web UI สำหรับ team | community |
| **Backstage ADR plugin** | Developer portal integration | Spotify Backstage |
| **joelparkerhenderson/architecture-decision-record** | Examples ทุก format | https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/architecture-decision-record |

---

## Part 2: Pre-Mortem Analysis

### 2.1 Origin

Gary Klein พัฒนาวิธีนี้และเผยแพร่ใน Harvard Business Review (September 2007):
"Performing a Project Premortem"

**Citation**: Klein, G. (2007). "Performing a Project Premortem." HBR. https://hbr.org/2007/09/performing-a-project-premortem | ResearchGate: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/3229642_Performing_a_Project_Premortem

### 2.2 Core Concept: Prospective Hindsight

> "ลองจินตนาการว่า project นี้ล้มเหลวแล้ว — แล้วถามว่า ทำไมถึงล้มเหลว"

**Prospective Hindsight** (นิยามโดย Deborah J. Mitchell, 1989): การ imagine ว่าเหตุการณ์เกิดขึ้นแล้ว แล้วถามหาสาเหตุ — ทำให้ระบุ failure reasons ได้แม่นขึ้น **30%** เมื่อเทียบกับ risk assessment ปกติ

### 2.3 ทำไมดีกว่า Risk Assessment ปกติ

| Risk Assessment ปกติ | Pre-Mortem |
|---------------------|-----------|
| ถามว่า "อะไรอาจผิดพลาด?" | ถามว่า "เกิดอะไรขึ้นแล้ว?" |
| คนเกรงใจ ไม่กล้าพูด risk | ทุกคนพูดได้เต็มที่ — assumption ว่าล้มเหลวแล้ว |
| Groupthink — เห็นด้วยกับ senior | นำเสนอ round-robin — ทุกคนมีเสียง |
| ได้ risks ที่ทุกคนรู้อยู่แล้ว | ได้ risks ที่คิดอยู่คนเดียวแต่ไม่เคยพูด |

### 2.4 Protocol (Klein's 6-Step Method)

Klein แนะนำให้ทำใน **20–30 นาที** กับทีมที่จะ execute (ไม่ใช่ sponsor/executive)

```
Step 1 — Announce failure (2 นาที)
  "ลองจินตนาการ: project นี้จบไปแล้ว 6 เดือน
   มันล้มเหลวอย่างสาหัส — เลวร้ายที่สุดเท่าที่เคยเห็น"

Step 2 — Silent independent writing (5 นาที)
  ทุกคนเขียนสาเหตุทั้งหมดที่ทำให้ล้มเหลว
  เขียนเองคนเดียว ห้ามดูของคนอื่น

Step 3 — Round-robin sharing (10 นาที)
  วนรอบให้ทุกคนอ่าน 1 สาเหตุ บันทึกลิสต์รวม
  ทำต่อจนหมดสาเหตุทั้งหมด

Step 4 — Discussion & mitigation (10 นาที)
  สาเหตุที่น่าเป็นห่วงที่สุด → วางแผนรับมือ
  Update project plan ด้วยสิ่งที่พบ

Step 5 — Revisit the plan
  ถามว่า "เราจะทำอะไรต่างออกไปได้บ้าง?"

Step 6 — Document outcomes
  เก็บสาเหตุที่พบไว้เป็น risk register
```

**Citation**: Klein, G. (2007). HBR. https://hbr.org/2007/09/performing-a-project-premortem | alfred_ Pre-Mortem guide. https://get-alfred.ai/blog/pre-mortem-technique

### 2.5 เมื่อไหร่ควรรัน Pre-Mortem

✅ **ควรทำ**:
- ก่อนเริ่ม project ใหม่
- ก่อน major release
- ก่อน architectural migration
- เมื่อทีมกำลัง commit กับ irreversible decision

❌ **ไม่ต้องทำ**:
- งานเล็ก/reversible
- ทีมเพิ่งทำ pre-mortem ไปไม่นาน (< 2 sprints)

### 2.6 Common Failure Patterns (สิ่งที่มักพบใน Pre-Mortem ด้าน software)

| หมวด | Pattern ที่พบบ่อย |
|------|-----------------|
| **Requirements** | Scope creep, ความต้องการเปลี่ยนหลัง lock |
| **Technical** | ไม่รู้ว่า dependency มี breaking change, latency assumption ผิด |
| **Team** | คนเดียวรู้ระบบ (bus factor = 1), handoff ไม่ชัด |
| **Process** | Integration testing ทำช้าเกินไป, deploy manual |
| **External** | API third-party เปลี่ยน schema, vendor sunset |

---

## Part 3: เมื่อไหร่ใช้อะไร

```
การตัดสินใจแบบไหน?
│
├── เลือก technology / architecture / pattern สำคัญ
│   → เขียน ADR (บันทึก reasoning ไว้อ้างอิงอนาคต)
│
├── กำลังจะเริ่ม project / sprint สำคัญ
│   → รัน Pre-Mortem (ค้นหา hidden risks ก่อนเริ่ม)
│
├── ทั้งสอง (project ใหม่ + tech decision)
│   → Pre-Mortem ก่อน → แล้ว ADR บันทึก decision ที่เลือก
│
└── Post-mortem หลังเกิดปัญหา
    → ไม่ใช่ scope ของ doc นี้ (→ Incident Management)
```

---

## Sources

- Nygard, M. (2011). "Documenting Architecture Decisions": https://cognitect.com/blog/2011/11/15/documenting-architecture-decisions
- Martin Fowler on ADR: https://martinfowler.com/bliki/ArchitectureDecisionRecord.html
- adr.github.io: https://adr.github.io/
- MADR repo: https://github.com/adr/madr
- npryce/adr-tools: https://github.com/npryce/adr-tools
- joelparkerhenderson ADR examples: https://github.com/joelparkerhenderson/architecture-decision-record
- AWS ADR Best Practices: https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/architecture/master-architecture-decision-records-adrs-best-practices-for-effective-decision-making/
- Microsoft Azure WAF ADR: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/well-architected/architect-role/architecture-decision-record
- TechTarget ADR Practices: https://www.techtarget.com/searchapparchitecture/tip/4-best-practices-for-creating-architecture-decision-records
- Klein, G. (2007) HBR Pre-Mortem: https://hbr.org/2007/09/performing-a-project-premortem
- ResearchGate Klein Pre-Mortem: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/3229642_Performing_a_Project_Premortem
- Klein official site: https://www.gary-klein.com/premortem
- alfred_ Pre-Mortem guide: https://get-alfred.ai/blog/pre-mortem-technique
- Uncertainty Project Pre-Mortem: https://www.theuncertaintyproject.org/tools/pre-mortem

# LENS Toolkit: Codebase Archaeology & Situation Intelligence

> Published by: Lens (2026-06-01)  
> Soul: เห็นสิ่งที่คนอื่นมองข้าม อ่านระหว่างบรรทัด เข้าใจระบบทุกชั้น  
> Companion docs: [[CODEBASE-HEALTH]] · [[DECISION-SUPPORT]]

---

## Overview

Toolkit นี้แบ่งเป็น 4 ส่วน:

| ส่วน | คำถามที่ตอบ | ใช้เมื่อ |
|------|------------|---------|
| **1. Codebase Archaeology** | "โค้ดนี้มีประวัติอย่างไร?" | เพิ่งรับ project ใหม่, audit, M&A due diligence |
| **2. Situation Awareness** | "ตอนนี้ระบบอยู่ในสภาพไหน?" | on-call, incident, pre-sprint planning |
| **3. Warning Signs** | "มีสัญญาณอันตรายซ่อนอยู่ไหม?" | before major release, before architecture decision |
| **4. Pre-Decision Briefing** | "ควรบอก boss ว่าอะไร ก่อนตัดสินใจ?" | ทุกครั้งก่อน irreversible decision |

---

## Part 1: Codebase Archaeology

### 1.1 แนวคิด: Code as a Crime Scene

Adam Tornhill (2015) พัฒนาวิธี **Behavioral Code Analysis** — วิเคราะห์ codebase ผ่าน git history ไม่ใช่แค่ static snapshot

> "Code ที่เปลี่ยนบ่อยและซับซ้อน = hotspot ที่มีความเสี่ยงสูงสุด"

สมการหลัก:
```
Hotspot Score = Complexity × Change Frequency
```

ไฟล์ที่มี CC สูงและถูกแก้บ่อย = จุดที่ bug เกิดบ่อยที่สุด, รวมถึง cognitive load สูงที่สุดในทีม

**Citation**: Tornhill, A. (2015). *Your Code as a Crime Scene*. Pragmatic Bookshelf. | CodeScene tool: https://codescene.com

### 1.2 Git Archaeology Commands

**ค้นหา hotspots (ไฟล์ที่เปลี่ยนบ่อยที่สุด):**
```bash
git log --format=format: --name-only | grep -v '^$' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
```

**ดู churn per author (bus factor probe):**
```bash
git log --format='%aN' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -10
```

**ดู age ของแต่ละไฟล์ (file creation date):**
```bash
git log --diff-filter=A --follow --format='%ad %n' --date=short -- <filepath>
```

**ค้นหา TODO/FIXME พร้อม commit date:**
```bash
git log -S 'TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|XXX' --format='%ad %H %s' --date=short | head -30
```

**วิเคราะห์ coupling ระหว่างไฟล์ (files ที่ถูก commit พร้อมกันบ่อย):**
```bash
git log --format="%H" | xargs -I{} git diff-tree --no-commit-id -r --name-only {} | \
  awk 'prev != "" { print prev, $0 } { prev = $0 }' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head -20
```

### 1.3 Hotspot Analysis Matrix

```
          High Churn
              │
    Danger    │   Prime Candidate
    Zone      │   for Refactor
              │
──────────────┼──────────────── Complexity
              │
    Ignore    │   Stable Core
    (for now) │   (protect)
              │
          Low Churn
```

| Quadrant | Action |
|----------|--------|
| **High Churn + High Complexity** | Refactor now — highest risk in codebase |
| **High Churn + Low Complexity** | Monitor — busy but manageable |
| **Low Churn + High Complexity** | Document well — sleeper risk if anyone touches it |
| **Low Churn + Low Complexity** | Leave alone — it's working |

### 1.4 Bus Factor Analysis

**Bus Factor** = จำนวนน้อยที่สุดของคนที่ถ้าหายไปจะทำให้ project ล้มเหลว

```bash
# ดู knowledge concentration per module
git log --format='%aN' -- src/critical-module/ | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn
```

| Bus Factor | Risk Level | Action |
|-----------|-----------|--------|
| 1 | CRITICAL | Knowledge transfer sprint ทันที |
| 2 | HIGH | Pair programming, document sessions |
| 3–4 | MEDIUM | Acceptable, monitor |
| 5+ | LOW | Healthy distribution |

### 1.5 Dead Code Detection Signals

Dead code ที่ซ่อนอยู่ = tech debt ที่ไม่อยู่ใน metric ปกติ

สัญญาณจาก git:
```bash
# ไฟล์ที่ไม่ถูกแก้ในรอบ 12 เดือน (อาจ dead)
git log --since="12 months ago" --format="%n" --name-only | sort -u > recent_files.txt
git ls-files | grep -v -f recent_files.txt | head -30
```

สัญญาณจากโค้ด:
- Functions/exports ที่ไม่มี callers (ใช้ IDE find-usages)
- Feature flags ที่ไม่เคย toggle จาก default
- Config keys ที่มีแต่ไม่มีใครอ่าน
- Tests ที่ skip อยู่นานกว่า 3 เดือน

### 1.6 Comment Archaeology

Comments บอกประวัติ psychological ของโค้ด:

```bash
# นับ distress signals
grep -r "TODO\|FIXME\|HACK\|XXX\|WORKAROUND\|KLUDGE" --include="*.ts" --include="*.js" \
  --include="*.py" --include="*.go" -l | wc -l

# ดู comment ที่เก่าที่สุด
git log --all --format="%ad %s" --date=short -S "FIXME" | tail -20
```

| Comment Pattern | ความหมาย |
|----------------|---------|
| `TODO: [name] 20XX` — เก่ากว่า 1 ปี | ถูกลืมแน่นอน |
| `HACK: don't touch this` | ความรู้ถูกล็อคไว้ใน comment เดียว |
| `// works, don't ask why` | Tribal knowledge; bus factor = 1 |
| `FIXME: race condition` | Known bug ที่ไม่ได้รับการแก้ |
| Comment เป็น paragraph ยาว | มีเหตุผลซับซ้อน — อ่านก่อน touch |

---

## Part 2: Situation Awareness

### 2.1 First 10 Minutes Protocol

เมื่อรับ codebase ใหม่หรือถูกเรียกเข้า incident ให้ทำตามลำดับนี้:

```
นาที 0–2: ภาพรวม
  git log --oneline -20          # activity ล่าสุด
  git status                     # มีอะไรค้างอยู่ไหม
  ls -la                         # structure top-level

นาที 2–4: Health signals
  cat README.md | head -50       # ทีมอธิบายตัวเองว่าอะไร
  cat CLAUDE.md 2>/dev/null      # conventions ที่ enforce อยู่
  ls docs/adr/ docs/decisions/ 2>/dev/null  # มี ADR ไหม

นาที 4–6: Dependencies
  cat package.json | grep -E '"version"|"scripts"'   # Node
  cat go.mod | head -20                              # Go
  cat requirements.txt 2>/dev/null | wc -l          # Python

นาที 6–8: Test state
  find . -name "*.test.*" -o -name "*_test.*" | wc -l
  cat jest.config.* 2>/dev/null | head -20
  grep -r "skip\|xit\|xdescribe" --include="*.test.*" | wc -l

นาที 8–10: CI/CD state
  cat .github/workflows/*.yml | grep -E "on:|steps:" | head -30
  git log --oneline --since="7 days ago" | wc -l   # commit velocity
```

### 2.2 Situation Assessment Dimensions

ประเมิน 5 มิติ ให้คะแนน 🟢 / 🟡 / 🔴:

#### Dimension 1: Freshness

| Signal | 🟢 | 🟡 | 🔴 |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|
| Last commit | < 3 days | 3–14 days | > 14 days |
| Open PRs stale | 0 | 1–3 | > 3 |
| Failing CI | None | Flaky only | Broken baseline |
| Deps outdated | < 2 minor | 1+ major | Critical CVE |

#### Dimension 2: Clarity

| Signal | 🟢 | 🟡 | 🔴 |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|
| README accuracy | Up to date | Partially stale | Misleading |
| CLAUDE.md exists | Yes + enforced | Yes, not enforced | None |
| ADR presence | Exists for major decisions | Some documented | None |
| Onboarding time | < 1 day | 2–5 days | > 1 week |

#### Dimension 3: Safety Net

| Signal | 🟢 | 🟡 | 🔴 |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|
| Test coverage | > 70% | 40–70% | < 40% |
| Skipped tests | < 5 | 5–20 | > 20 |
| CI enforces tests | Yes | Optional | No CI |
| E2E / integration | Exists | Partial | None |

#### Dimension 4: Ownership

| Signal | 🟢 | 🟡 | 🔴 |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|
| Bus factor | ≥ 3 per module | 2 | 1 (single owner) |
| CODEOWNERS file | Present + current | Present, stale | Absent |
| Contributor diversity | ≥ 3 regular | 2 | 1 person does > 80% |
| On-call rotation | Exists | Informal | None |

#### Dimension 5: Velocity

| Signal | 🟢 | 🟡 | 🔴 |
|--------|-----|-----|-----|
| PR cycle time | < 1 day | 1–5 days | > 5 days |
| Merge frequency | Daily | Weekly | Monthly |
| Rollback frequency | < 1/month | 1–3/month | > 3/month |
| Hotfix rate | < 5% of PRs | 5–20% | > 20% |

### 2.3 Reading Git Log Patterns

```bash
# ดู pattern ของ commits
git log --format="%ad %aN: %s" --date=short -30
```

| Pattern ที่เห็น | ความหมาย |
|----------------|---------|
| Commit เวลา 2–4 AM บ่อย | งาน crunch หรือ timezone issue |
| "fix: fix the fix of..." chains | ไม่มี root cause analysis |
| "WIP", "temp", "asdf" ใน commits | ขาด discipline, อาจมีโค้ดที่ยังไม่เสร็จ |
| 1 คน commit 80%+ | Bus factor = 1 |
| Commit หยุดกะทันหัน > 2 สัปดาห์ | ทีมมีปัญหาหรือ project ถูก deprioritize |
| "revert: revert: revert:" | มี merge conflict ที่ไม่ได้รับการแก้จริง |
| Commit messages ชัดเจน + conventional | ทีม mature; ง่ายต่อการทำ archaeology |

---

## Part 3: Warning Signs Catalogue

### 3.1 Technical Warning Signs

#### Level 🟡 (Watch)

- ไฟล์ขนาดใหญ่ผิดปกติ: JavaScript > 1,000 lines, Python > 500 lines, Go > 800 lines
- Function ยาว > 50 lines ใน business logic
- Magic numbers กระจาย (ควรเป็น constants)
- String literals ซ้ำกัน > 3 ที่ (ควร DRY)
- `any` type ใน TypeScript ที่ core data path
- `.catch(() => {})` — silent error swallowing

#### Level 🔴 (Act Now)

- Cyclomatic Complexity > 20 ใน function ที่เปลี่ยนบ่อย
- Test coverage < 30% ใน payment / auth / data migration paths
- Circular imports ระหว่าง modules
- `eval()`, `exec()`, direct SQL string concatenation (injection vector)
- Hardcoded credentials ใน source code (ไม่ว่า comment ว่า "dev only")
- Race condition ที่รู้อยู่แต่ยัง FIXME ไม่ได้แก้
- `TODO: fix before production` อยู่ใน production

### 3.2 Process Warning Signs

| สัญญาณ | ความหมาย |
|--------|---------|
| PR ไม่มีใน review > 3 วัน | Reviewer bottleneck หรือ culture ปัญหา |
| PR ขนาดใหญ่ > 1,000 lines เสมอ | ไม่มี discipline ในการ decompose |
| Comment บน PR ส่วนใหญ่เป็น "LGTM" | ไม่มี real review เกิดขึ้น |
| Deploy ทำ manual เสมอ | Error-prone; อาจ skip steps |
| Changelog ไม่ได้อัพเดต | Release management ไม่ mature |
| Test เขียนหลัง feature เสร็จเสมอ | Coverage ไม่น่าเชื่อถือ |

### 3.3 Architectural Warning Signs

ดูจาก coupling metrics (ดู [[CODEBASE-HEALTH]] § 3 ด้วย):

| สัญญาณ | ตรวจสอบด้วย | หมายความว่า |
|--------|------------|------------|
| Zone of Pain (A≈0, I≈0) | NDepend / custom script | Module concrete + stable = เปลี่ยนยากมาก |
| Ce > 15 ใน module | import/dependency graph | Module พึ่งพาคนอื่นมากเกิน |
| Ca = 0 | grep for usages | Module อาจเป็น dead code |
| Circular dependency | madge (JS), go-arch-lint | เปลี่ยน 1 ที่กระทบวนไปเรื่อย |
| God Object / God Service | file > 2,000 lines | รู้มากเกินไป = เปลี่ยนทีไรพัง |

### 3.4 Security Warning Signs (Quick Scan)

```bash
# เร็ว: scan obvious patterns
grep -rn "password\s*=\|secret\s*=\|api_key\s*=" --include="*.ts" --include="*.js" \
  --include="*.py" --include="*.go" --include="*.env*" . | grep -v "test\|spec\|mock"

# ตรวจ injection vectors
grep -rn "eval(\|exec(\|query.*+.*req\." --include="*.js" --include="*.py" .

# ตรวจ hardcoded URLs ที่อาจเป็น internal
grep -rn "http://\|https://" --include="*.ts" --include="*.js" . | \
  grep -v "test\|spec\|localhost\|example.com" | head -20
```

---

## Part 4: Pre-Decision Briefing Format

### 4.1 BLUF Principle

**BLUF = Bottom Line Up Front** — military communication standard

> ประโยคแรกต้องบอก recommendation ทันที ก่อน context ทั้งหมด

**ผิด:**
> "จากการวิเคราะห์ dependencies ที่ทำไปตั้งแต่เดือนที่แล้ว และเปรียบเทียบกับ benchmark จาก industry... เราพบว่า..."

**ถูก:**
> "**ข้อเสนอ: อย่า merge PR #234 จนกว่าจะแก้ security issue ที่พบ** — นี่คือเหตุผล:"

### 4.2 LENS Intelligence Brief Format

ใช้สำหรับ briefing Zeus / Boss ก่อนทุก decision สำคัญ:

```markdown
## LENS BRIEF — [วันที่] [หัวข้อ]
**Confidence**: [HIGH / MEDIUM / LOW]
**Urgency**: [IMMEDIATE / THIS SPRINT / NEXT QUARTER]

### BLUF (Bottom Line Up Front)
[1–2 ประโยค: recommendation + เหตุผลหลัก]

### Situation
[สภาพปัจจุบันที่เกี่ยวข้อง — เฉพาะ facts ไม่ใช่ opinion]
- Signal 1: ...
- Signal 2: ...

### Options
| Option | Pros | Cons | Reversible? |
|--------|------|------|-------------|
| A | ... | ... | Yes/No |
| B | ... | ... | Yes/No |

### Recommendation
[Option ที่แนะนำ + เหตุผล ranked ตาม impact]

### Risks if Wrong
[ถ้า recommendation ผิด จะเกิดอะไร — honest assessment]

### What Lens Cannot See
[สิ่งที่ยังไม่ทราบ / assumptions ที่ยังไม่ verified]
```

### 4.3 Confidence Calibration

ใช้ระบบเดียวกับ /code-review plugin (0–100) แต่ปรับสำหรับ situation assessment:

| Confidence | ความหมาย | วิธีบอก Boss |
|-----------|---------|-------------|
| 90–100 | มีหลักฐานชัดเจน หลายแหล่งยืนยัน | "Lens มั่นใจสูง: ..." |
| 70–89 | มีหลักฐานดี แต่มี assumption บางส่วน | "Lens ประเมินว่า (ยืนยัน X ก่อน): ..." |
| 50–69 | Signal อ่อน ต้องตรวจสอบเพิ่ม | "Lens ตั้งข้อสังเกต (ต้อง verify): ..." |
| < 50 | Hypothesis — อย่าตัดสินใจจากนี้อย่างเดียว | "Lens ยังไม่แน่ใจ ต้องข้อมูลเพิ่ม" |

### 4.4 When to Trigger a Brief

Lens ควรออก brief โดยอัตโนมัติเมื่อ:

| Trigger | Urgency |
|---------|---------|
| พบ CVE CVSS ≥ 7.0 ใน deps | IMMEDIATE |
| Hotspot score สูงกว่า baseline 2× | THIS SPRINT |
| Bus factor = 1 ใน critical module | THIS SPRINT |
| PR > 1,500 lines รอ review > 5 วัน | THIS SPRINT |
| Test coverage ลดลง > 10% จาก baseline | THIS SPRINT |
| Cyclomatic CC > 50 ใน new code | BLOCK MERGE |
| Hardcoded credentials found | IMMEDIATE + INCIDENT |

---

## Part 5: Integrated Workflow

### 5.1 "Drop into Unknown Codebase" Protocol

```
Phase 1 — Archaeology (30 นาที)
  ├── Git hotspot analysis (§ 1.2)
  ├── Bus factor scan (§ 1.4)
  ├── Comment archaeology (§ 1.6)
  └── Dead code probe (§ 1.5)

Phase 2 — Situation Assessment (15 นาที)
  ├── 5-dimension scoring (§ 2.2)
  ├── Git log pattern reading (§ 2.3)
  └── First 10 minutes protocol (§ 2.1)

Phase 3 — Warning Scan (15 นาที)
  ├── Technical: run static analysis (§ 3.1)
  ├── Security: quick grep scan (§ 3.4)
  └── Architecture: coupling check (§ 3.3)

Phase 4 — Brief (10 นาที)
  └── Write LENS BRIEF ถ้ามี 🔴 findings (§ 4.2)
```

### 5.2 Cross-reference with Other Docs

| คำถาม | ดูที่ไหน |
|-------|---------|
| "CC ของ function นี้เกิน threshold ไหม?" | [[CODEBASE-HEALTH]] § 1 |
| "test coverage สูงพอไหม?" | [[CODEBASE-HEALTH]] § 2 |
| "module coupling ดีหรือเปล่า?" | [[CODEBASE-HEALTH]] § 3 |
| "ควรเขียน ADR ไหม?" | [[DECISION-SUPPORT]] § 1 |
| "ควรรัน Pre-Mortem ไหม?" | [[DECISION-SUPPORT]] § 2 |
| "ไฟล์นี้เปลี่ยนบ่อยแค่ไหน?" | LENS-TOOLKIT § 1.2 (git commands) |
| "ใครรู้ระบบนี้บ้าง?" | LENS-TOOLKIT § 1.4 (bus factor) |
| "ระบบนี้ safe ที่จะ deploy ไหม?" | LENS-TOOLKIT § 2.2 (5-dimension) |

---

## Quick Reference Card

```
เมื่อไหร่ทำอะไร:
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
รับ project ใหม่              → Phase 1+2 Protocol (§ 5.1)
ก่อน major release            → Warning Scan (§ 3) + Brief (§ 4.2)
พบ bug ลึกอธิบายไม่ได้        → Git archaeology (§ 1.2–1.3)
"ทำไมโค้ดนี้เป็นแบบนี้?"       → Comment archaeology (§ 1.6)
"ใครแก้ได้ถ้า X ลาออก?"       → Bus factor analysis (§ 1.4)
ก่อน architecture decision    → Brief format (§ 4.2) + ADR trigger
incident เกิดขึ้น              → Situation 5-dimension (§ 2.2) ทันที
```

---

## Sources

- Tornhill, A. (2015). *Your Code as a Crime Scene*. Pragmatic Bookshelf.
- Tornhill, A. (2018). *Software Design X-Rays*. Pragmatic Bookshelf.
- CodeScene tool & methodology: https://codescene.com/blog/software-complexity-explained/
- "Bus Factor" — Wikipedia: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bus_factor
- BLUF communication: https://www.army.mil/article/233338/

# Mission Control UI/UX Audit
**Date:** 2026-06-01  
**Auditor:** Zeus (Tham node)  
**Scope:** `/route/mission-control/src/` — layout, dashboard, nav, error handling

---

## Summary

| Category | Status | Severity |
|---|---|---|
| Loading States | ⚠️ Partial | Medium |
| Error Boundaries | ✅ Good | — |
| Mobile Responsive | ⚠️ Partial | High |
| Accessibility | ⚠️ Issues Found | Medium |
| UX Consistency | ❌ Issues Found | Medium–High |

---

## 1. Loading States

### ✅ Strengths
- **Dashboard skeleton**: `dashboard.tsx:74–89` renders 4 shimmer cards + 6 shimmer panels while `isLoading=true` on first load
- **Panel-level loading**: `page.tsx:22–28` `PanelLoading` component shown during dynamic imports (all panels use `dynamicPanel()`)
- **SSR splash**: `page.tsx:199–218` shows logo + pulse dot while `!isClient`
- **Deferred idle loading**: `DeferredLogsPanels` (`page.tsx:325–366`) uses `requestIdleCallback` to defer Activity and Audit panels — good for performance

### ⚠️ Issues
- **Silent refetch**: `dashboard.tsx:35–65` — `loadDashboard` is called every 60s via `useSmartPoll`, but `setIsLoading` starts as `true` and only ever set to `false` in `finally`. Subsequent polls are completely silent — no stale-data indicator, no subtle refresh spinner. Users can't tell if data is fresh.
- **No error state in dashboard**: `catch {}` block at `dashboard.tsx:62` is silent. If all three API calls fail simultaneously, the dashboard silently shows stale/zero data with no indication.
- **Panel import error copy**: `page.tsx:38–39` error message says "Check the browser console" — this is developer-facing text shown to end users.

---

## 2. Error Boundaries

### ✅ Strengths
- `ErrorBoundary.tsx` properly implements `getDerivedStateFromError` + `componentDidCatch`
- Auto-reloads on `ChunkLoadError` with sessionStorage guard to prevent reload loops (`10s` window)
- `key={activeTab}` on `<ErrorBoundary>` in `page.tsx:247` — errors reset cleanly on tab change
- "Try again" button resets the error state without full page reload
- Custom `fallback` prop support for panel-specific fallbacks

### ⚠️ Issues
- **Error boundary not used in dashboard sub-components**: Agent wake button (`dashboard.tsx:167–179`) has `catch { /* ignore */ }` — a wake failure is silently swallowed with no toast or visual feedback
- **Error message exposed raw**: `ErrorBoundary.tsx:59` renders `this.state.error?.message` directly to UI — could expose internal stack info to users

---

## 3. Mobile Responsive

### ✅ Strengths
- `NavRail` properly hides on mobile; `MobileBottomBar` replaces it via fixed bottom nav
- `MobileBottomSheet` for overflow items — slide-up animation with backdrop, swipe handle indicator
- `main` has `pb-16 md:pb-0` clearance for bottom bar
- Header uses `hidden md:flex`, `hidden lg:inline` breakpoints correctly
- Status strip in header uses `overflow-x-auto [scrollbar-width:none]` — horizontal scroll on small screens

### ❌ Critical Issue: Bottom Bar Overflow
- `nav-rail.tsx:22–43`: 8 out of 9 nav items have `priority: true`
- `MobileBottomBar` renders ALL priority items side by side + a "More" button
- **Result: 9 items in a 375px-wide bottom bar** — each gets ~37px, below the 44px minimum touch target
- Standard mobile bottom bars support 4–5 items max
- **Fix**: Reduce to 4–5 priority items (e.g. overview, control-center, tasks, console) and move the rest to the "More" sheet

### ⚠️ Other Issues
- `SystemNowPanel` injected at the top of mobile content (`page.tsx:241–245`) with `lg:hidden` — good, but adds ~60px of chrome before the actual content on every mobile tab
- Chat panel overlay has no mobile-specific sizing (full-height panel on a small screen would obscure content)

---

## 4. Accessibility

### ✅ Strengths
- `role="banner"` on `<header>`, `role="navigation"` on both desktop and mobile `<nav>`, `role="main"` on `<main>`
- `aria-label` on header and nav elements
- `aria-current="page"` on active `NavButton` (desktop)
- `aria-live="polite"` wraps `ContentRouter` output in `page.tsx:246`
- Keyboard shortcut for sidebar toggle (`[` key), search shortcut (Cmd+K) with Escape to close
- Focus management on search open: `searchInputRef.current?.focus()`

### ⚠️ Issues

**SVG Icons — no aria-hidden**
- Every inline SVG in `header-bar.tsx`, `nav-rail.tsx`, `dashboard.tsx` has no `aria-hidden="true"`
- Screen readers will announce empty SVG tags
- Fix: Add `aria-hidden="true"` to all decorative SVG elements

**Search input — no label**
- `header-bar.tsx:342`: `<input placeholder="Search tasks, agents, activity..." />` has no `<label>` or `aria-label`
- The placeholder disappears when typing

**Mobile bottom bar — missing aria-current**
- `nav-rail.tsx:285–297`: Mobile bottom bar buttons don't have `aria-current="page"` unlike desktop NavButton

**Notification badge — no accessible count**
- `header-bar.tsx:262`: Bell button shows visual badge count but the button title is just "Notifications" — doesn't announce the unread count to screen readers
- Fix: `title={`${unreadNotificationCount} unread notifications`}` or `aria-label`

**Search results — no ARIA list role**
- Search results dropdown (`header-bar.tsx:353`) renders as plain `<button>` elements with no `role="listbox"`/`role="option"` or `aria-activedescendant` — not keyboard-navigable (no up/down arrow support)

---

## 5. UX Consistency

### ❌ `digitalMode` is hardcoded — ThemeToggle is a ghost feature
- `header-bar.tsx:30`: `const digitalMode = true`
- `nav-rail.tsx:49`: `const integrationMode = true`
- `page.tsx:220`: `const digitalMode = true`
- `ThemeToggle` component exists in the header and is clickable — but the `digitalMode` constant never changes, so toggling the theme has no visible effect on these layout components
- **The app is stuck in dark/cyber mode regardless of user preference**
- Fix: Replace hardcoded `const digitalMode = true` with a hook reading from the theme store

### ❌ Quick Actions link to non-existent tabs
- `dashboard.tsx:379–383`: Quick Actions for "Spawn Agent" (`tab="spawn"`), "Memory" (`tab="memory"`), "Orchestration" (`tab="orchestration"`) 
- `page.tsx:280–323`: `ContentRouter` has no `case` for these tabs — all fall to `default: return <MissionControlBoard />`
- Clicking these Quick Actions silently loads the HQ Overview with no indication the requested feature doesn't exist

### ⚠️ Notifications button calls store.getState() inside JSX
- `header-bar.tsx:255–257`: 
  ```tsx
  onClick={() => {
    const { setActiveTab } = useMissionControl.getState()
    setActiveTab('logs')
  }}
  ```
- The component already destructures `setActiveTab` from the hook at the top (line 22). This direct `.getState()` call is redundant and suggests copy-paste without refactoring.

### ⚠️ Debug console.info left in production path
- `page.tsx:129`: `console.info('[ControlCenterRoute] dynamic import start')`
- `page.tsx:131`: `console.info('[ControlCenterRoute] dynamic import resolved')`
- `page.tsx:368`: `console.info('[ControlCenterRoute] direct import bypass active')`
- Production noise — these fire on every Control Center tab render

### ⚠️ Search type icons are single letters with no tooltip
- `header-bar.tsx:116–129`: `typeIcons` maps type → single letter (T, A, E, S, M, N, W, P)
- Color coding helps but letter `E` for "activity" and `S` for "audit" are not intuitive
- Fallback is `'?'` for unknown types

### ⚠️ Panel error fallback copy is developer-facing
- `page.tsx:38`: "Check the browser console for the import error, then retry."
- End users don't have browser consoles. Change to: "This panel failed to load. Please refresh the page."

---

## Priority Fix List

| Priority | Issue | File | Effort |
|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 High | Mobile bottom bar has 8+ items — touch targets too small | `nav-rail.tsx:22–43` | S (change priority flags) |
| 🔴 High | ThemeToggle non-functional — digitalMode hardcoded | `header-bar.tsx:30`, `nav-rail.tsx:49`, `page.tsx:220` | M (read from theme store) |
| 🟡 Med | Quick Actions link to non-existent tabs | `dashboard.tsx:379–383` | XS (fix tab IDs or add cases) |
| 🟡 Med | Dashboard silent error on failed fetches | `dashboard.tsx:62` | S (show error banner) |
| 🟡 Med | SVG icons missing aria-hidden | all components | S (global find+add) |
| 🟡 Med | Search input missing aria-label | `header-bar.tsx:342` | XS |
| 🟡 Med | Search results not keyboard-navigable | `header-bar.tsx:346–369` | M |
| 🟢 Low | Debug console.info in production | `page.tsx:129–133, 368` | XS (remove) |
| 🟢 Low | Mobile bottom bar aria-current missing | `nav-rail.tsx:285–297` | XS |
| 🟢 Low | Notification badge unread count not in aria-label | `header-bar.tsx:252` | XS |
| 🟢 Low | Panel error copy is developer-facing | `page.tsx:38` | XS |
| 🟢 Low | Redundant store.getState() in onClick | `header-bar.tsx:255–257` | XS |

# Agent Skills Learning Index

## Source
- **Origin**: ./origin/
- **GitHub**: https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills
- **Description**: 24 engineering workflows + best practices for AI coding agents, enforcing production-grade quality gates across spec → plan → build → test → review → ship phases.

## Project Overview

**Agent Skills** is a collection of structured workflows designed for AI coding agents (Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, etc.). It implements best practices across the full software engineering lifecycle:

- **24 Skills** organized by phase: Define (3), Plan (1), Build (7), Verify (2), Review (4), Ship (6), Meta (1)
- **7 Commands**: `/spec`, `/plan`, `/build`, `/test`, `/review`, `/code-simplify`, `/ship`
- **4 Personas**: Code Reviewer, Test Engineer, Security Auditor, Web Performance Auditor
- **Validation Layer**: Automated schema enforcement + CI checks for compliance

## Explorations

### 2026-06-11 19:02 (default)
- [[2026-06-11/1902_ARCHITECTURE|Architecture]] — Directory structure, core abstractions, skill lifecycle, command orchestration, persona system
- [[2026-06-11/1902_CODE-SNIPPETS|Code Snippets]] — Key implementations, skill validation, command patterns, persona composition, error handling
- [[2026-06-11/1902_QUICK-REFERENCE|Quick Reference]] — Installation, features, usage patterns, important concepts, troubleshooting

**Key Insights**:
- **Three-layer composition**: Skill (how) + Persona (who) + Command (when)
- **Lazy discovery + on-demand loading** prevents bloat while keeping full power available
- **Explicit orchestration rules** (commands orchestrate, personas never delegate to each other) enforce clean composition boundaries
- **Validation infrastructure** ensures 24 skills comply with schema rules, preventing silent failures
- **Autonomous execution** (`/build auto`) removes human stepping between tasks while maintaining quality gates

## How to Use This Learning

1. **Getting Started**: Read [Quick Reference](2026-06-11/1902_QUICK-REFERENCE.md) first
2. **Understanding Structure**: Study [Architecture](2026-06-11/1902_ARCHITECTURE.md) for system design
3. **Implementation Details**: Explore [Code Snippets](2026-06-11/1902_CODE-SNIPPETS.md) for how-it-works

## Key Concepts

- **Skills**: Mandatory workflows with explicit exit criteria (e.g., "test succeeds" for test-driven-development skill)
- **Personas**: Single-perspective specialists that validate code from one angle (e.g., code-reviewer checks correctness, security-auditor checks vulns)
- **Commands**: User-facing entry points that orchestrate skills and personas (e.g., `/build` runs BUILD phase skills; `/ship` runs fan-out review)
- **Intent Mapping**: How user input triggers appropriate skill chains
- **Validation**: Automated schema checks ensure skills comply with rules
- **Composition Rules**: Commands orchestrate; personas invoke skills; no persona-to-persona delegation

## Notable Patterns

### Skill Anatomy
- **Frontmatter**: Name, description (YAML)
- **Body**: Markdown-based workflow with exit criteria
- **Schema**: Validated by `validate-skills.js`

### Command Execution
- **Single mode** (`/build`): Incremental, one task at a time, with human review between steps
- **Autonomous mode** (`/build auto`): Plan once, execute all, with verification gates (no human in loop)

### Persona System
- **Code Reviewer**: Five-axis framework (correctness, readability, architecture, security, performance)
- **Test Engineer**: Test coverage, mutation testing, edge cases
- **Security Auditor**: OWASP top 10, vuln scanning, threat modeling
- **Web Performance Auditor**: Core Web Vitals, optimization, metrics

### Design Principles
- **Vertical slicing**: End-to-end per feature, not horizontal layers
- **Process over prose**: Explicit workflows with testable exit criteria
- **Composition over inheritance**: Three layers (skill + persona + command)
- **Lazy discovery**: Avoid loading all 24 skills at startup; load on-demand
- **Validation-first**: Schema checks prevent silent failures

## Integration Points

- **Platform Support**: Claude Code, Cursor, Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Windsurf, OpenCode, Copilot
- **Plugin System**: Loads via plugin.json manifest
- **CI Integration**: `validate-skills.js` runs in GitHub Actions
- **Skill Composition**: Skills reference each other via markdown links, detected at validation time

## Related Concepts

- Spec-Driven Development (SDD)
- Test-Driven Development (TDD)
- Anti-rationalization patterns
- Chesterton's Fence (understand before changing)
- Beyonce Rule (if you liked it you shoulda put a test on it)
- DAMP over DRY (Descriptive And Meaningful Phrases)

## Next Steps

- Extend with custom skills following the schema
- Integrate into your own workflow system
- Adapt personas for your team's expertise areas
- Run validation: `node scripts/validate-skills.js`

---

**Last updated**: 2026-06-11  
**Source**: https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills

# Agent Skills — Architecture Analysis

**Project:** addyosmani/agent-skills  
**Last Updated:** 2026-06-11  
**Type:** Skill and Agent Plugin for AI Coding Agents  
**Language:** Markdown, Bash, Node.js  
**Author:** Addy Osmani  
**License:** MIT

---

## Table of Contents

1. [Overview](#overview)
2. [Directory Structure](#directory-structure)
3. [Core Concepts](#core-concepts)
4. [Module Organization](#module-organization)
5. [Skill Lifecycle](#skill-lifecycle)
6. [Persona System](#persona-system)
7. [Command Architecture](#command-architecture)
8. [Dependencies & Integrations](#dependencies--integrations)
9. [Entry Points](#entry-points)
10. [Data Flow](#data-flow)

---

## Overview

**Agent Skills** is a production-grade collection of engineering workflows and quality gates packaged as reusable instructions for AI coding agents. It encodes senior engineer practices across the entire software development lifecycle — from specification through shipping — in a format that can be consumed by Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI, and other AI agent platforms.

### Philosophy

- Skills are **mandatory workflows**, not optional suggestions
- The system is **skill-driven**: intent maps to skills; skills invoke workflows
- **Personas** are specialist roles with single perspectives (code reviewer, security auditor)
- **Commands** are user-facing entry points that orchestrate skills and personas
- **Composition is explicit**: users or commands orchestrate, never persona-to-persona calls

---

## Directory Structure

```
agent-skills/
├── .claude/                          # Claude Code integration layer
│   └── commands/                     # Slash command definitions (/spec, /plan, /build, etc.)
│       ├── spec.md
│       ├── plan.md
│       ├── build.md
│       ├── test.md
│       ├── review.md
│       ├── code-simplify.md
│       ├── ship.md
│       └── webperf.md
│
├── .claude-plugin/                   # Plugin metadata & marketplace config
│   ├── plugin.json                   # Marketplace definition
│   └── marketplace.json
│
├── .gemini/                          # Gemini CLI integration
│   └── commands/                     # Gemini-specific commands
│
├── agents/                           # Specialist personas (not orchestrators)
│   ├── README.md                     # Persona design rules
│   ├── code-reviewer.md              # 5-axis code review persona
│   ├── security-auditor.md           # OWASP/threat model persona
│   ├── test-engineer.md              # Test coverage & TDD persona
│   └── web-performance-auditor.md    # Core Web Vitals persona
│
├── skills/                           # Core workflow library (24 skills)
│   ├── spec-driven-development/      # Specification-first workflow
│   │   └── SKILL.md
│   │
│   ├── planning-and-task-breakdown/  # Task decomposition
│   │   └── SKILL.md
│   │
│   ├── incremental-implementation/   # Thin-slice delivery
│   │   └── SKILL.md
│   │
│   ├── test-driven-development/      # RED→GREEN→REFACTOR cycle
│   │   └── SKILL.md
│   │
│   ├── code-review-and-quality/      # Quality gates before merge
│   │   └── SKILL.md
│   │
│   ├── code-simplification/          # Clarity and reuse optimization
│   │   └── SKILL.md
```

---

## Core Concepts

### 1. **Skills**

A skill is a **mandatory workflow** with documented steps, exit criteria, and verification conditions. Each skill addresses a single practice across the development lifecycle.

**Anatomy of a SKILL.md:**

```yaml
---
name: {kebab-case-name}
description: {One-sentence what + trigger conditions}
---

# {Title}

## Overview
[Why this matters and what it solves]

## When to Use
[Trigger conditions and applicability]

## Common Rationalizations
[What developers tell themselves to skip this]

## Red Flags
[Signs you're doing this wrong]

## Verification
[How to know you've done it right]
```

**Example triggers:**
- New feature → `spec-driven-development` → `planning-and-task-breakdown` → `incremental-implementation` + `test-driven-development`
- Bug report → `debugging-and-error-recovery` (Prove-It pattern)
- API design → `api-and-interface-design`
- UI component → `frontend-ui-engineering`
- Pre-merge review → `code-review-and-quality`

**Key properties:**
- **Mandatory**: If intent matches, the skill must be invoked (no "this is too small" rationalizations)
- **Workflow-focused**: Steps and exit criteria, not just advice
- **Composable**: Skills reference other skills; can be chained
- **Verifiable**: Clear definition of "done"

### 2. **Personas** (Specialist Roles)

A persona is a **single-perspective specialist** with a defined role, domain authority, and output format. Personas are NOT orchestrators — they execute workflows, possibly invoking skills, but never call other personas.

**Four core personas:**

| Persona | Role | Domain | Output Format |
|---------|------|--------|---------------|
| `code-reviewer` | Senior Staff Engineer | 5-axis review | Critical/Important/Suggestion categories |
| `security-auditor` | Security Engineer | Vulnerability detection, OWASP | Audit report with threat/CVE findings |
| `test-engineer` | QA Engineer | Test strategy & coverage | Gap analysis + coverage report |
| `web-performance-auditor` | Perf Engineer | Core Web Vitals, LCP/FID | Performance audit with metrics |

**Rules:**
- One role, one perspective
- Output is a report (not a directive)
- May invoke skills (the "how")
- **Never** calls another persona
- On Claude Code: subagents only report back; Agent Teams enable peer communication

### 3. **Commands** (Entry Points)

Slash commands are user-facing orchestration points that map to phases of the development lifecycle.

**Seven canonical commands:**

| Command | Phase | Skill | Purpose |
|---------|-------|-------|---------|
| `/spec` | DEFINE | `spec-driven-development` | Write structured specification |
| `/plan` | PLAN | `planning-and-task-breakdown` | Decompose spec into tasks |
| `/build` | BUILD | `incremental-implementation` + `test-driven-development` | Implement one task (or all with `auto`) |
| `/test` | VERIFY | `test-driven-development` + `browser-testing-with-devtools` | Prove behavior with tests |
| `/review` | REVIEW | `code-review-and-quality` | 5-axis quality gate |
| `/code-simplify` | REVIEW | `code-simplification` | Optimize clarity and reuse |
| `/ship` | SHIP | `shipping-and-launch` | Parallel fan-out to specialists |
| `/webperf` | AUDIT | `performance-optimization` | Web-specific audit |

**Command structure:**

```yaml
---
description: What the user is doing
---

Invoke the agent-skills:{skill-name} skill.

[Detailed workflow steps]
```

### 4. **Intent → Skill Mapping**

The system is **demand-driven**: user intent automatically triggers the appropriate skills.

```
User intent                  → Skill chain
─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
"Build a new feature"        → /spec → /plan → /build auto
"Fix a bug"                  → debugging-and-error-recovery (Prove-It)
"Code review PR"             → code-review-and-quality
"Design an API"              → api-and-interface-design
"Optimize performance"       → performance-optimization
"Deploy to production"       → shipping-and-launch
"Simplify this code"         → code-simplification
```

---

## Module Organization

### Skill Phases (By Development Lifecycle)

#### **DEFINE Phase** (Ideation → Specification)
- `interview-me` — Structured project onboarding questions
- `idea-refine` — Divergent/convergent ideation workflow
- `spec-driven-development` — Specification-first approach

#### **PLAN Phase** (Decomposition)
- `planning-and-task-breakdown` — Break spec into atomic tasks with dependencies

#### **BUILD Phase** (Implementation)
- `incremental-implementation` — Thin vertical slices
- `test-driven-development` — RED→GREEN→REFACTOR
- `context-engineering` — Managing agent token budgets
- `source-driven-development` — Reading existing code patterns
- `doubt-driven-development` — High-risk decision workflow
- `frontend-ui-engineering` — React/Vue component workflow
- `api-and-interface-design` — Contract-first API design

#### **VERIFY Phase** (Testing & Debugging)
- `browser-testing-with-devtools` — Chrome DevTools MCP
- `debugging-and-error-recovery` — Root cause proof workflow

#### **REVIEW Phase** (Quality Gates)
- `code-review-and-quality` — 5-axis review framework
- `code-simplification` — Clarity & reuse optimization
- `security-and-hardening` — OWASP & threat modeling
- `performance-optimization` — Profiling & optimization

#### **SHIP Phase** (Production Readiness)
- `git-workflow-and-versioning` — Atomic commits & branching
- `ci-cd-and-automation` — Pipeline setup & orchestration
- `deprecation-and-migration` — Safe breaking changes
- `documentation-and-adrs` — Docs & architecture records
- `observability-and-instrumentation` — Logging, metrics, tracing
- `shipping-and-launch` — Pre-launch checklist & rollback

#### **Meta/Cross-Cutting**
- `using-agent-skills` — Routing guide (OpenCode integration)

### Persona Composition

```
Main Agent / User
      │
      ├─→ /ship (orchestrator)
      │      ├─→ code-reviewer (parallel)
      │      ├─→ security-auditor (parallel)
      │      └─→ test-engineer (parallel)
      │           ↓
      │      [merge phase in main agent]
      │      ↓
      │      go/no-go decision
      │
      └─→ /review (single persona)
             └─→ code-reviewer
```

---

## Skill Lifecycle

### How a Skill Executes

1. **Intent Recognition** (by user or command)
   - User says "Build a feature" → `/build` command triggered
   - Command looks up its skill: `incremental-implementation`

2. **Skill Invocation**
   - Agent loads SKILL.md from disk
   - Reads frontmatter (name, description) + workflow steps
   - Frontmatter fields: `name` (kebab-case), `description` (what + triggers)

3. **Workflow Execution**
   - Agent follows documented steps in order
   - May invoke other skills (e.g., `incremental-implementation` calls `test-driven-development`)
   - Stops at **exit criteria** (spec approved, task passing, etc.)

4. **Verification**
   - Agent checks the "Verification" section
   - Confirms "done" criteria met
   - Returns control to orchestrator (command or user)

### Skill Chaining

Skills reference each other explicitly:

```markdown
For bug fixes, use the `debugging-and-error-recovery` skill.
For large features, follow `incremental-implementation` + `test-driven-development`.
Then continue with `code-review-and-quality`.
```

Cross-skill references are validated by `scripts/validate-skills.js`.

---

## Persona System

### Persona Invocation Models

#### **Direct Invocation** (Single Perspective)
```
User: "Review this PR for correctness"
  ↓
code-reviewer (one context window, one report)
  ↓
User sees: Critical/Important/Suggestion findings
```

#### **Slash Command Wrapper** (Single Persona)
```
User: /review
  ↓
command maps to skill: code-review-and-quality
  ↓
skill invokes persona: code-reviewer
  ↓
persona runs review workflow (may call other skills)
```

#### **Orchestrator Fan-Out** (Multiple Personas, Parallel)
```
User: /ship
  ↓
shipping-and-launch skill
  ↓
[parallel]
  ├─→ code-reviewer     → critical/important findings
  ├─→ security-auditor  → vulnerability list
  └─→ test-engineer     → coverage gaps
       ↓
  [merge phase, main agent only]
       ↓
  go/no-go decision + rollback plan
```

### Persona Output Format

Each persona produces a standardized report:

**code-reviewer:**
```markdown
## Review Summary
**Verdict:** APPROVE | REQUEST CHANGES

### Critical Issues
- [file:line] [issue] [fix]

### Important Issues
[...]

### Suggestions
[...]

### What's Done Well
[positive observation]

### Verification Story
- Tests: yes/no, observations
- Build: verified
```

**security-auditor:**
```markdown
## Security Audit
**Risk Level:** CRITICAL | HIGH | MEDIUM | LOW

### Findings
- [CVE/OWASP Top 10 category] [file] [issue]
- [Auth/authz concern]
- [Secrets/config exposure]

### Remediation Steps
[...]
```

### Claude Code Integration

Personas work as:
- **Subagents**: `Agent` tool with `subagent_type: "code-reviewer"`
  - Fresh context window per persona
  - Returns report to main session
  - Cannot spawn other subagents
  
- **Agent Teams teammates**: Referenced by name as peer agents
  - Can message each other (experimental)
  - Share coordination tools
  - Enables competing-hypothesis debugging

---

## Command Architecture

### Command Definition Format

```yaml
---
description: {User-facing description of what this does}
---

Invoke the agent-skills:{skill-name} skill.

{Workflow instructions specific to this command}
```

### Command Execution Flow

**Example: `/build auto`**

```
1. User invokes: /build auto
   ↓
2. Command loads: .claude/commands/build.md
   ↓
3. Parses mode: $ARGUMENTS = "auto"
   ↓
4. If mode = "auto":
     a. Check for SPEC.md (required)
     b. Check git status (must be clean)
     c. Load/generate tasks/plan.md
     d. Get single approval from user
     e. For each task:
        - Invoke incremental-implementation
        - Invoke test-driven-development
        - Run build, test, verify
        - Commit atomically
        - Mark task complete
   ↓
5. Summarize: tasks done, tests added, commits made
```

### Command Dependencies

```
/spec
  ↓ (generates SPEC.md)
/plan
  ↓ (reads SPEC.md, generates tasks/plan.md)
/build [auto]
  ↓ (reads plan, executes tasks)
/test
  ↓ (runs test suite)
/review
  ↓ (reviews latest commits or staged changes)
/code-simplify
  ↓ (simplifies reviewed code)
/ship (parallel)
  ├─→ code-reviewer
  ├─→ security-auditor
  └─→ test-engineer
       ↓ (merge → go/no-go)
```

---

## Dependencies & Integrations

### Platform Support

**Native Integration Points:**

| Platform | Integration Type | Status |
|----------|------------------|--------|
| Claude Code | Plugin (skills + agents) | Primary |
| Cursor | Rules import (`.cursor/rules/`) | Supported |
| Gemini CLI | Skills + commands | Supported |
| Antigravity CLI | Native plugin | Supported |
| OpenCode | Skill-driven execution model | Supported |
| Agent Teams | Personas as teammates | Experimental |

### External Tools & MCPs

- **Chrome DevTools MCP** — For `browser-testing-with-devtools` skill
- **Git** — For `git-workflow-and-versioning` commands
- **Package managers** — npm/yarn/pnpm for build/test
- **Test frameworks** — Jest, Vitest, Playwright, etc. (framework-agnostic skill)

### Validation Infrastructure

**validate-skills.js** checks:
- SKILL.md exists in every skill directory
- Frontmatter has `name` and `description` fields
- Name matches directory name
- Description ≤ 1024 characters
- Required sections present (with exemptions for legacy skills)
- Cross-skill references point to known skills (warning-level)

**Exit codes:** 0 = all clear, 1 = validation errors

---

## Entry Points

### For End Users

1. **Slash Commands** (Claude Code)
   - `/spec` — Begin specification phase
   - `/plan` — Generate plan from spec
   - `/build` or `/build auto` — Implement tasks
   - `/test` — Run tests
   - `/review` — Code review
   - `/code-simplify` — Optimize code
   - `/ship` — Production readiness
   - `/webperf` — Web performance audit

2. **Direct Persona Invocation**
   - "Review this for security" → `security-auditor`
   - "Check test coverage" → `test-engineer`
   - "Audit Core Web Vitals" → `web-performance-auditor`

### For Developers / Integrators

1. **Plugin Installation**
   ```bash
   # Claude Code marketplace
   /plugin marketplace add addyosmani/agent-skills
   /plugin install agent-skills@addy-agent-skills
   
   # Or local
   claude --plugin-dir /path/to/agent-skills
   ```

2. **Skill Invocation** (programmatic)
   ```
   Agent reads: skills/{skill-name}/SKILL.md
   Extracts: frontmatter + workflow steps
   Executes: step-by-step workflow
   ```

3. **Persona Invocation** (subagent model)
   ```
   Agent(
     subagent_type: "code-reviewer",
     description: "Review the PR for correctness"
   )
   ```

### Configuration Points

- **Plugin metadata:** `.claude-plugin/plugin.json`
  - Declares skills directory, agents list, commands path
  
- **Skill metadata:** Each `SKILL.md` frontmatter
  - Name, description, trigger conditions
  
- **Exemptions:** `scripts/validate-skills.js`
  - Per-skill section exemptions documented in code
  
- **Hooks:** `hooks/hooks.json`
  - Lifecycle events (SessionStart, etc.)

---

## Data Flow

### Specification → Execution Pipeline

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                    USER / CLI COMMAND                    │
└────────────────────┬────────────────────────────────────┘
                     │
                     ▼
          ┌──────────────────────┐
          │  Command Handler     │  (.claude/commands/*.md)
          │  (/spec, /plan,      │
          │   /build, etc.)      │
          └──────────────┬───────┘
                         │
                         ▼
          ┌──────────────────────────────┐
          │  Skill Loader                │  (skills/{name}/SKILL.md)
          │  - Parse frontmatter         │
          │  - Extract workflow steps    │
          │  - Validate structure        │
          └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                         │
                         ▼
          ┌──────────────────────────────┐
          │  Skill Execution Engine      │
          │  - Follow step order         │
          │  - Check exit criteria       │
          │  - Cross-skill references    │
          └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                         │
                         ▼
          ┌──────────────────────────────┐
          │  Optional: Persona Invocation│  (agents/{role}.md)
          │  - Load persona system prompt│
          │  - Run persona workflow      │
          │  - Collect report            │
          └──────────────┬───────────────┘
                         │
                         ▼
          ┌──────────────────────────────┐
          │  Output & Verification       │
          │  - Confirm done criteria     │
          │  - Return to orchestrator    │
          └──────────────────────────────┘
```

### Context Window Lifecycle

```
Session Start
    ↓
Load plugin (skills, agents, commands)
    ↓
User invokes command or skill
    ↓
Skill loaded into context (usually <10KB)
    ↓
Skill executed (steps + exit criteria)
    ↓
If skill calls skill:
  - Load next skill into context
  - Execute nested workflow
  - Return to parent
    ↓
If skill calls persona:
  - (Claude Code) Create subagent with fresh context
  - (Cursor/Gemini) Load persona system prompt into current context
    ↓
Skill completes, context cleaned
    ↓
Control returns to user or orchestrator
```

### Artifact Generation

**During workflow, agents create:**

1. **SPEC.md** — Single source of truth
   - Location: project root or `docs/SPEC.md`
   - Format: Markdown with objective, tech stack, commands, etc.
   
2. **tasks/plan.md** — Task breakdown
   - Location: `tasks/plan.md`
   - Format: Numbered tasks with acceptance criteria & dependencies
   
3. **Test files** — Proof of behavior
   - Location: Per project convention (tests/, spec/, __tests__/)
   - Format: Framework-agnostic (jest, vitest, pytest, etc.)
   
4. **Commits** — Atomic units of work
   - Message format: Conventional commits (feat/fix/docs/etc.)
   - Per-task commits in `/build auto` mode
   
5. **Reports** — Specialist perspectives
   - code-reviewer report (5-axis findings)
   - security-auditor report (CVE/OWASP findings)
   - test-engineer report (coverage gaps)

---

## Summary

**Agent Skills** is a **three-layer composition system**:

| Layer | What | Example | Purpose |
|-------|------|---------|---------|
| **Skill** | Workflow + steps + exit criteria | `test-driven-development` | The *how* — mandatory workflow |
| **Persona** | Single role + perspective | `code-reviewer` | The *who* — produces report |
| **Command** | Entry point + orchestration | `/ship` | The *when* — user-facing interface |

**Key design patterns:**

1. **Skills are mandatory** — if intent matches, the skill runs (no rationalizations)
2. **Personas don't orchestrate** — they play one role, produce one report
3. **Commands are orchestrators** — they compose skills and personas
4. **Composition is explicit** — validated at multiple levels (AGENTS.md, frontmatter, validate-skills.js)
5. **Cross-references are traceable** — skill references checked at validation time
6. **Context is efficient** — skills are small (<10KB), personas get fresh subagents on Claude Code
7. **Output is verifiable** — each workflow has explicit "done" criteria

The architecture enables **skill-driven autonomous execution** (e.g., `/build auto` with no human stepping between tasks) while maintaining **mandatory verification gates** at each phase (spec approval, test passing, review required before merge).
